chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Ḥamzah, from Abān ibn Muṣʿab, from Yūnus ibn Ẓabyān, or al-Muʿallā ibn Khunays, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, “What do you have from this earth?” So he smiled, then said:

Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام and commanded him to split open eight rivers in the earth with his big toe. Among them are Sayḥān and Jayḥān, and it is the river of Balkh, and al-Khushūʿ, and it is the river of al-Shāsh, and Mihrān, and it is the river of India, and the Nile of Egypt, and the Tigris, and the Euphrates.

So whatever these water, or from which water is drawn, is for us; and whatever is for us is for our Shiʿah. And our enemy has no share in it except what he has usurped from it. And indeed our friend is surely in a far more expansive domain in what lies between this and this,” meaning between the heaven and the earth.
Then he recited this verse: “Say: They are for those who believe in the life of this world—usurped from them—while they shall be exclusively theirs on the Day of Resurrection, without usurpation.”

key_terms.أَنْهَارٍ: rivers, presented here as sources of life and provision
key_terms.الْأَرْضِ: the earth as a domain of divinely assigned possession and authority
key_terms.الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection, when rights are fully and purely realized
key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلَ: Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام, the angel sent by Allah to bring about the rivers
key_terms.غَصَبَ: usurped, referring to wrongful seizure of what is not rightfully theirs
key_terms.لِشِيعَتِنَا: for our Shiʿah, indicating their share through allegiance to the Imam
key_terms.وَلِيَّنَا: our friend or loyal adherent, aligned with the Imam

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the Imam’s relationship to the earth and the believers’ share in worldly blessings?
ai.summary: This hadith presents the earth and its life-giving resources as belonging by divine designation to the Imam and, through that, to the Shiʿah. It also applies a Quranic statement to the condition of believers in this world, portraying their worldly share as subject to usurpation now but as purely theirs on the Day of Resurrection.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah Bin Ahmad, from Ali Bin Al Numan, from Salih Bin Hamza, from Aban Bin Mus’ab, from Yunus Bin Zabyan, or al Moalla Bin Khunays who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, ‘What have you all (Imams<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>) to do from the earth?’ So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> smiled, then said:

‘Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Blessed and High Sent Jibraeel<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> and Commanded him<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> that he<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> furrows eight rivers by his<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> big toe in the earth – from these is Sayhan, and Jayhan, and it is the river Balkh, and Al-Khashou, and it is River Shash, and Mihran, and it is a river of India, and Nile of Egypt, and Dajla, and Euphrates.

So whatever is watered from or drawn, so it is for us<sup>asws</sup>, and whatever was for us<sup>asws</sup> so it is for our<sup>asws</sup> Shias, and there isn’t anything from it for our<sup>asws</sup> enemies except what they have usurped upon, and that our<sup>asws</sup> friends would be in (a place) more capacious in what is between this to this, meaning between the sky and the earth’.
Then heasws recited this Verse [7:32] Say: These are for the Believers in the life of this world the ones usurped upon especially on the Day of Judgement without being usurped’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Abdallah ibn Ahmad from Ali ibn al-Ni‘man from Salih ibn Hamza from Aban ibn Mus‘ab from Yunus ibn Zabyan or al-Mu‘alla ibn al-Khnith who has said the following.
“I asked abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.), ‘What is for you from this earth?” He smiled and then said,

“Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, sent Jibril and commanded him to dig with his toe eight rivers on earth. Of these are the River Sayhan and Jayhan which is the River in Balkh (central Asia) the River al-Khshu‘ which is the River al-Shash, river Mihran which is India, River Nile in Egypt, Tigris and Euphrates.

All that these rivers provide water or all that take water from them belong to us and whatever is for us is for our Shi‘a. There is nothing for our enemies except what they have usurped. Our friends and supporters in an place bigger than this and this, the sky and earth.

The Imam (a.s.) then recited the words of Allah. “They are made for the believers in this world (but others have usurped it from them) and are exclusively for them in the life hereafter (no one would usurp from them).” [7:32]
